'''Gennady''' (or '''Gennadii''' or '''Gennadiy''') '''Semenovich Makanin''' (1938–2017) was a Russian mathematician, awarded the 2010 I. M. Vinogradov Prize for a series of papers on the problem of algorithmically recognizing the solvability of arbitrary equations in free groups and semigroups.

==Education and career==
At [[Moscow State University]] he received his undergraduate degree and in 1967 his Russian [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree (PhD). His dissertation К проблеме тождества в конечно-определённых группах и полугруппах (On the identity problem in finitely-presented groups and semigroups) was supervised by [[Andrey Markov Jr.]] and [[Sergei Adian]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=168222}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |title=A translation of G. S. Makanin's 1966 Ph.D. thesis "On the Identity Problem for Finitely Presented Groups and Semigroups|author=Nyberg-Brodda, Carl-Fredrik|year=2021|class=math.GR|eprint=2102.00745}}</ref>

Makanin spent his career (since 1966) working at the Steklov Institute of Mathematics (since 2013 as a freelance employee). From the Steklov Institute of Mathematics he received in 1977 his Russian [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree (similar to [[habilitation]]) with dissertation Проблема разрешимости уравнений в свободной полугруппе (The problem of solvability of equations in a free semigroup). On the basis of his 1977 dissertation he was an invited speaker at the 1978 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Helsinki.<ref>{{cite web|title=Makanin, G. S.|website=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Makanin}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.ams.org/books/trans2/117/|title=Eight Lectures Delivered at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Helsinki, 1978|series=American Mathematical Society Translations: Series 2|year=1981|volume=117|publisher=American Mathematical Society|doi=10.1090/trans2/117|isbn=9780821830697|mr=665105}} {{ISBN|978-0-8218-3069-7}} (print); {{ISBN|978-1-4704-3328-4}} (online)</ref>

He gained international recognition for his research on combinatorial group theory and algorithmic problems in the theory of semigroups. [[Zlil Sela]], [[Eliyahu Rips]], and others have made important applications of Makanin-Razborov diagrams to [[geometric group theory]].

In 1982 Makanin published a complete solution (an algorithm with proof of validity) to the problem of recognizing the solvability of equations in a [[free group]]. An English translation was published in 1983.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Makanin, Gennady S.|title=Equations in a free group|journal=Mathematics of the USSR-Izvestiya|volume=21|issue=3|year=1983|pages=483–|doi=10.1070/IM1983v021n03ABEH001803|bibcode=1983IzMat..21..483M|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1070/IM1983v021n03ABEH001803/meta|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1984 (followed by English translation in 1985) he published a proof, using techniques similar to those in his 1982 paper, of the decidability, for any free group, of two different formal theories generated by that free group.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Makanin, Gennadiı Semyonovich|title=Decidability of the universal and positive theories of a free group|journal=Mathematics of the USSR-Izvestiya|volume=25|issue=1|year=1985|page=75|doi=10.1070/IM1985v025n01ABEH001269|bibcode=1985IzMat..25...75M|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1070/IM1985v025n01ABEH001269/meta|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Remarks on Makanin's research==
[[Martin Davis (mathematician)|Martin Davis]] and [[Julia Robinson]] worked unsuccessfully on the problem which was eventually solved in 1977 by Makanin:
{{blockquote|We worked together on a problem on which we didn’t get anywhere. We were trying to prove the unsolvability of the decision problem for [[word equation|word equations]]. It turned out that we wouldn’t have been able to do that because the problem is solvable. Makanin solved it positively. That had a curious relationship to [[Hilbert's tenth problem|Hilbert’s Tenth Problem]], because some of the Russians were interested in proving it unsolvable because its unsolvability would have been a way to get the unsolvability of Hilbert’s Tenth Problem, without proving my conjecture, which they thought was likely false. But in fact, it turned out to be on the other side of the line.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Jackson, Allyn|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200805/ |title=An interview with Martin Davis |journal=Notices of the AMS |volume=55 |number=5 |date=May 2008 |pages=560–571}} (quote from Martin Davis, p. 565)</ref>}}

[[Yuri Matiyasevich]] published a generalization of what he called the "celebrated theorem of G. S. Makanin about decidability of word equations".<ref>{{cite book|author=Matiyasevich Y.|year=1997|contribution=Some decision problems for traces|editor1= Adian S.|editor2= Nerode A.|title= Logical Foundations of Computer Science. LFCS 1997|series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 1234|volume=1234 |pages=248–257|publisher=Springer|location=Berlin; Heidelberg|doi=10.1007/3-540-63045-7_25 |isbn=978-3-540-63045-6 }}</ref>
